intro: Mexico City rewards visitors with world-class museums, street food and layered history at every turn. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: 12 lines, M$5-6 per ride, 05:00-00:00 weekdays; very crowded at rush hour.
Metrobús BRT and trolleybuses cover many main avenues; pay with a rechargeable card.
Taxis are white and magenta; agree the fare or use the meter, and prefer sitio stands at night.
Uber, DiDi and inDrive work widely and are cheap; check the plate before getting in.
Driving is slow and parking is hard; walking is best in Centro, Roma and Condesa.
Bikes: EcoBici bike-share has stations in central areas; helmets are not common.

zocalo.name: Zocalo (Plaza de la Constitución)
zocalo.hours: Open 24 hours · flag ceremony around 08:00 and 18:00 (check on the day)
zocalo.tip: It is one of the largest squares in the world, so wear a hat and bring water; the plaza is exposed and hot at midday.

catedral.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City
catedral.price_text: Free entry · small fee for the tower tour (check on the day)
catedral.tip: The building is sinking slowly, so look at the floor levels; dress modestly and stay quiet during services.

palacio-nacional.name: National Palace
palacio-nacional.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00 · closed when official events happen (check on the day)
palacio-nacional.tip: The Diego Rivera murals on the main staircase are the highlight; bring your passport or ID or you may be turned away.

castillo.name: Chapultepec Castle
castillo.price_text: Around MXN 90–110 for adults · free on Sundays for Mexican residents (check on the day)
castillo.tip: It sits on a hill, so take the short shuttle or walk up slowly; the terrace view over the city is the reward.

antropologia.name: National Museum of Anthropology
antropologia.price_text: Around MXN 90–110 for adults · free on Sundays for Mexican residents (check on the day)
antropologia.tip: The Aztec Sun Stone is in the first rooms; pick two or three halls instead of trying to see everything.

frida.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul)
frida.price_text: Around MXN 250–350 · buy online in advance (check on the day)
frida.tip: Tickets sell out days ahead, so book a timed slot online and arrive a little early.

guadalupe.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
guadalupe.landmark: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
guadalupe.tip: It is an active pilgrimage site, so dress modestly and keep quiet; the old basilica next door is also worth a look.

templo-mayor.name: Templo Mayor
templo-mayor.price_text: Around MXN 80–100 for adults (check on the day)
templo-mayor.tip: The ruins sit right beside the cathedral, so pair the two; the small museum holds the best finds.

bellas-artes.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
bellas-artes.price_text: Around MXN 80–100 for the museum · performances priced separately (check on the day)
bellas-artes.tip: Look up at the glass roof and the murals; check the evening programme if you want a concert in the main hall.

angel.name: Angel of Independence
angel.price_text: Free to see from the street
angel.hours: Always visible · roundabout busy all day
angel.tip: It sits in the middle of a big roundabout, so view it from the Paseo de la Reforma sidewalk and cross only at lights.

vasconcelos.name: Biblioteca Vasconcelos
vasconcelos.tip: The floating shelves and glass walls are the draw; keep voices low as it is a working library.

aragon.name: Bosque de Aragón
aragon.tip: It is a large local park far from the centre, so go with a local or use a ride app and keep valuables out of sight.

pendulo.name: Cafebrería El Péndulo
pendulo.price_text: Coffee and a snack around MXN 100–200
pendulo.tip: It is a bookshop with a café, so it is a good rest stop after walking Roma; branches exist, so check which one you want.

barragan.name: Casa Luis Barragán
barragan.price_text: Around MXN 300–500 · guided visits only, book ahead (check on the day)
barragan.hours: Visits by reservation only · usually Tue–Sun (check on the day)
barragan.tip: You cannot walk in without a booking, so reserve online well ahead and arrive on time.

azteca.name: Estadio Azteca
azteca.price_text: Tour and match prices vary · check on the day
azteca.hours: Tours and matches on set dates only (check on the day)
azteca.tip: It is far south of the centre, so check whether a match or tour is running before you travel out.

imagic.name: Imagic Park
imagic.price_text: Ticket prices vary · check on the day
imagic.hours: Usually daily, hours vary (check on the day)
imagic.tip: It is a family play park on the city's west edge, so confirm opening hours and ticket prices before setting out.

kataplum.name: Kataplum
kataplum.price_text: Ticket prices vary · check on the day
kataplum.hours: Usually daily, hours vary (check on the day)
kataplum.tip: It is an indoor play centre aimed at children, so check age rules and prices online first.

lago-mayer.name: Lago Mayer, Alameda Oriente
lago-mayer.price_text: Free entry · some activities cost extra
lago-mayer.tip: It is a big park with a lake on the eastern edge of the city, so plan transport and go in daylight.

revolucion.name: Monument to the Revolution
revolucion.price_text: Free to see · small fee for the lift to the top (check on the day)
revolucion.hours: Monument open daily · lift hours vary (check on the day)
revolucion.tip: Take the lift inside for a city view, and go at night when the dome is lit.

postal.name: Palacio Postal
postal.hours: Weekdays roughly 08:00–20:00 · Sat shorter (check on the day)
postal.tip: It is still a working post office, so walk in quietly and look up at the golden staircase.

mineria.name: Palacio de Minería
mineria.price_text: Free entry · some exhibitions charge (check on the day)
mineria.tip: The stone courtyard and staircase are the highlight; check if a book fair or exhibition is on.

francisco-villa.name: Parque Francisco Villa
francisco-villa.tip: It is a small neighbourhood park, good for a short rest between Roma and Condesa walks.

mercado-merced.name: Mercado de la Merced
mercado-merced.tip: It is a huge, busy market, so go with a local or a guide, keep cash small and watch your bag.

torre-latino.name: Mirador Torre Latinoamericana
torre-latino.tip: Go up on a clear day for the view over the Zocalo and the volcanoes; skip it in smog or rain.

xochimilco.name: Xochimilco trajinera boat ride
xochimilco.price_text: Boats hired per hour, around MXN 500–700 per boat (check on the day)
xochimilco.tip: The price is per boat, not per person, so share with a group; agree the price and time before boarding.

coyoacan-walk.name: Coyoacán neighbourhood walk
coyoacan-walk.price_text: Free · cafés and markets cost extra
coyoacan-walk.hours: Best in daylight · plaza lively all day
coyoacan-walk.tip: Wander from the main plaza to the market for churros and tostadas, then rest in the shaded square.

roma-walk.name: Roma and Condesa street walk
roma-walk.hours: Streets open all day · cafés roughly 08:00–22:00
roma-walk.tip: Walk the leafy streets between Parque México and Parque España, and stop for coffee and tacos along the way.

tacos-tour.name: Street taco and market food tour
tacos-tour.price_text: Around MXN 700–1200 per person (check on the day)
tacos-tour.tip: A guided tasting is the easiest way to try many stalls safely; say yes to the spicy salsa only if you mean it.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Zócalo, the great museums and the floating gardens of Xochimilco.

styles.label: Food

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Aztec ruins, colonial churches and the pyramids at Teotihuacán.

stays.why: Walk to the Zócalo, Templo Mayor and Bellas Artes. Busy by day, quieter at night; use sitio taxis after dark.
Leafy streets, cafés and bars; good for food and nightlife. Easy walking, short ride apps to the center.
Upscale hotels near Chapultepec Park and the anthropology museum. Calm and walkable, pricier restaurants.
Colonial lanes, the Frida Kahlo house and markets. Slower pace; longer rides to the center.

food: Eat tacos al pastor from busy stalls; a few tacos cost M$60–120. Pick places with a crowd and turnover.
Markets are cheap and good: Mercado de San Juan and La Merced for produce, cheese and cooked food.
Try pozole, tamales, chilaquiles and tlayudas. Breakfast at a fonda is often M$80–150.
Drink only bottled or filtered water, and skip ice from street carts if your stomach is sensitive.
Book ahead for top restaurants in Roma and Polanco; walk-ins are hard on weekend nights.
more_time: Swap a city day for Teotihuacán: go early by bus or tour to climb the pyramids before the heat and crowds.
Add a day in Coyoacán for the Frida Kahlo museum (book tickets online) and the markets.
Take a boat (trajinera) at Xochimilco on a weekend; agree the price per boat before boarding.
